title: What’s been driving Western growth?
caption: Average industry contributions to real GDP growth in Western states, 2022–2024.
source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis; Lookout West.
alt: Heatmap of average contributions to real GDP growth, 2022–2024, by industry and Western state. Green indicates positive contributions and red indicates negative contributions; total growth appears below each state.

title: High beef prices, a smaller breeding herd
caption: Beef-cow inventory and inflation-adjusted retail beef prices have different observation dates; neither series measures ranch profits.
source: USDA NASS and ERS; BLS CPI-U via FRED; Lookout West. Retrieved September 9, 2026.
alt: Two line charts: U.S. beef-cow inventory falls to 27.6 million on January 1, 2026, while retail beef reaches $9.46 per pound in July 2026, in December 2025 dollars.

title: Cattle’s scale and local importance differ
caption: Cattle and calf sales across the 13-state West and six Plains states, alongside their share of each state’s farm receipts in 2025.
source: USDA ERS, Farm Income and Wealth Statistics, September 3, 2026 release; Lookout West calculations.
alt: Paired bar charts compare cattle sales and farm-receipt shares in 19 states. Nebraska leads sales at $20.34 billion; Wyoming has the highest cattle share of farm receipts at 77.7 percent.

title: A retained heifer takes years to add beef
caption: An illustrative retention decision in autumn 2026 can produce calf-sale revenue in autumn 2028, before the offspring supplies beef in late 2029. Timing is not a forecast.
source: Biological sequence adapted from Oklahoma State University Extension; Lookout West. Illustrative timing, not a forecast.
alt: Timeline: retain a heifer in autumn 2026, breed her in spring 2027, first calf born in spring 2028, sell the calf at weaning in autumn 2028, and offspring supplies beef in late 2029.

title: Tyson’s planned hubs sit in the feeding belt
caption: Selected facilities in Tyson’s August 13 announcement, with state cattle-on-feed inventories as of August 1. Plant symbols mark communities, not facility gates.
source: USDA NASS, August 21, 2026; Tyson Foods, August 13, 2026; U.S. Census Bureau 2025 community coordinates; Lookout West.
alt: Map shows planned core hubs in Dakota City, Nebraska; Holcomb, Kansas; and Amarillo, Texas. Pasco, Washington, is marked for sale, Eagle Mountain, Utah, for case-ready closure, and Joslin, Illinois, for slaughter closure. Nebraska, Kansas and Texas hold 65.1 percent of reported national feedlot inventory.

title: Drought repeatedly puts forage at risk
caption: Estimated national cattle exposure to drought, January 2010–September 1, 2026. Severe-or-worse drought is included within the moderate-or-worse total; exposure does not measure individual ranch losses.
source: U.S. Agricultural Commodities in Drought, USDA/NDMC; Lookout West. Retrieved September 9, 2026.
alt: Area chart of estimated U.S. cattle inventory exposed to drought. On September 1, 2026, 60 percent is exposed to moderate-or-worse drought, including 34 percent exposed to severe-or-worse drought.
